purpose: Synthetic-only multi-field claim plan, canonical-input, status privacy and semantic preflight fixtures. No cryptographic or issuer qualification is implied.

covers: as_of fresh within 300 seconds of verifier request issued_at, with 30-second future skew

negative.reason: The strict parser rejects integers outside the JCS exact safe-integer range before a generic JSON value or canonicalizer can round or reinterpret them.
W3C Bitstring Status List v1.1 Working Draft cannot be labelled a W3C Recommendation.
The source origin field must be an HTTPS origin, not a URL containing an application path.
Status evidence profile must explicitly require anti-rollback checking.
Duplicate JSON object member names violate the JCS/I-JSON input contract and cannot be safely detected after lossy object parsing.
RFC 6901 permits only ~0 and ~1 escapes in a JSON Pointer token; ~2 must reject before field selection.
A verifier challenge must expire strictly after its issue time; zero or negative validity windows are invalid.
A delegated TLSNotary notary attestation is not a self-contained public proof; its verification scope must retain the delegated notary trust assumption.
The canonical HTTPS origin port must be in the range 1..=65535; a five-digit lexical match is not sufficient.
Canonical HTTPS origin must omit default port 443.
When DNS server identity is the selected identity kind, it must exactly equal the canonical origin host.
The v1 canonical HTTPS origin profile admits lowercase ASCII DNS names only; IPv4/IPv6 address literals are outside the profile.

nonclaims: The fixture uses synthetic identifiers and zero digests.
No TLS session or proof is present.
All profile IDs are test labels, not qualified profiles.
Schema shape is not policy correctness or authorization.
The plan binds three fields from one synthetic response; it does not yet prove their transcript openings or predicate.
